_comment: Two design rules. In-KB questions are worded the way a customer would ask,
never the way the article is written, so retrieval has to do semantic work
rather than matching keywords. Out-of-KB questions are deliberately adjacent
to a real article rather than absurd, because 'who won the 1998 world cup' is
not what breaks a refusal guardrail. 'Is there a free trial' sitting next to
The set is split. 'tune' is what top_k and min_score were chosen against.
'holdout' was written first and left untouched during tuning, and is only
read by `evaluate.py --holdout`. Reporting scores on the set you tuned on
measures fit to that set, not generalisation, which is the whole reason the

_grounding_comment: A grounding check is a self-report, so measuring it on answers that are
already correct only shows it is agreeable. Each case pairs a correct
answer with a mutation of it, and the pair gives two numbers worth having:
how often the check flags something that was fine, and how often it misses
The mutations are one per failure class, not six of the same kind: a
changed figure, a dropped condition, a widened scope, an invented detail,
a flipped rule, and a plausible addition the articles never mention.

grounding_cases.correct: Annual plans are discounted 20% against monthly billing.
grounding_cases.mutated: Annual plans are discounted 25% against monthly billing.

grounding_cases.correct: Annual plans cancelled within 30 days of purchase are refunded in full.
grounding_cases.mutated: Annual plans are refunded in full whenever you cancel.

grounding_cases.correct: Only owners and admins can invite people.
grounding_cases.mutated: Owners, admins and members can all invite people.

grounding_cases.correct: The REST API is rate limited to 1,000 requests per hour per workspace.
grounding_cases.mutated: The REST API is rate limited to 1,000 requests per hour, and the limit can be raised on request.

grounding_cases.correct: Deleting a workspace removes all content after a 30-day grace period.
grounding_cases.mutated: Deleting a workspace removes all content immediately and cannot be undone.
Tessera targets 99.9% monthly uptime and credits are applied automatically.
